_about: Companion to architectural_refactor_2026-06-06_v2.md — full per-question decision rationale, cross-area conflict resolutions, user decisions needed, and the completeness-critique that produced the post-critique sections. Produced 2026-06-06 by an 8-area adversarially-verified investigation workflow.

decisions.question: §9 Q1 — Operation registry shape: OpRegistryEntry with function pointers, or methods on OperationConfig backed by a registry?
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: Option A/B hybrid. Phase 1 ships a DATA-ONLY `&'static [OpRegistryEntry]` table indexed by OperationType discriminant, holding `spec`, `&'static [ParamDef]`, and `ToolConstraints`. FeedsHints is NOT static data — it stays a `fn(&OperationConfig) -> FeedsHints` accessor because operation_feeds_hints projects per-op config fields (cfg.scallop_height, cfg.z_step, cfg.max_depth at feeds/suggest.rs:710-722). `generate: GenerateFn` and `compatibility: fn(CutterKind)` are DEFERRED to Phase 5 behind a parity gate. Generation stays in execute.rs's exhaustive match (compute/execute.rs:242, 23-arm, no wildcard) for Phase 1. Rationale: the data half already exists in exhaustive form split across spec()/param_defs_for_type/tool_constraints_for_type; consolidating it is lossless. The behavior half is not — execute_operation_annotated arms take a 15-arg context and each does bespoke span construction + per-op semantic annotate; a GenerateFn would have to re-match the variant internally, re-introducing the dispatch it removes.
decisions.dissent: none — op-registry, macro-prototype, and parity areas all independently reached A/B-hybrid-data-only. The only correction (FeedsHints is a fn accessor, not static data) was raised by both op-registry and suggest verification and is incorporated.

decisions.question: §9 Q2 — Central list: X-macro now, or keep hand-written exhaustive matches until after Phase 1?
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: Hand-written matches for Phase 1; introduce `for_each_op!` only in Phase 2, AFTER the OpRegistryEntry/spec-literal shape is frozen, and ONLY for pure-list/metadata derivations: OperationType decl, ALL, op_type(), new_default(), as_params/as_params_mut, plus a generated `category()` method. Do NOT macro-generate spec() bodies, param_defs arrays, OperationConfig, or execute.rs arms in Phase 2. The vetted prototype (compiling, 4/4 tests at /tmp/rscam_xmacro_proto) proves the list->enum/ALL/category/registry derivation is feasible with macro_rules! and zero new dependencies; malformed entries produce E0063/E0599/E0425/E0428 diagnostics that point at the list-entry line, not the macro body. Rationale: catalog.rs maintains ~12 parallel 23-arm enumerations; the pure lists are mechanical, high-value, low-readability-cost macro targets, while spec()/param_defs carry rich per-op data (9-field OperationSpec literals) that reads worse in a macro. Phase 1 first gives the macro a stable target.
decisions.dissent: none — op-registry and macro-prototype concur. Macro-prototype additionally proved (empirically) that a pure-macro const ALL_2D/ALL_3D split is impractical in macro_rules!; the resolution is to keep the consts hand-written and generate category() + a 3-way partition sync test.

decisions.question: §9 Q3 — Cutter API: is external MillingCutter implementation supported? If yes do not seal it; if no document the internal-only contract.
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: Treat MillingCutter as effectively internal; do NOT seal it in Phase 3 (sealing is churn with zero current external implementors), but DOCUMENT the asymmetry: external impls compile (pub trait at tool/mod.rs:149, pub ToolDefinition::new at tool/mod.rs:355) but are second-class — they cannot flow through build_cutter (closed ToolType match at compute/cutter.rs:9, exhaustive 5-arm) or any project/MCP IO path, only via manual ToolDefinition::new. Consequence for Phase 3: CutterKind conversions MUST be derivable from ToolGeometryHint (the universal signal every cutter yields via geometry_hint()), with ToolType->CutterKind as a convenience layered on top — NOT the primary path — so externally-implemented cutters still classify.
decisions.dissent: none — cutter and parity areas agree. All six in-tree `impl MillingCutter` are the five built-in cutters plus ToolDefinition; no external implementors exist.

decisions.question: §9 Q4 — Unknown project tool type: keep fallback-to-EndMill, warn, or fail load?
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: Warn-and-default-to-EndMill, and UNIFY the three divergent parsers first. Today: core project_file.rs:461 (lenient, _ => EndMill, custom strings ball_nose/ballnose...), viz io/project.rs:882 restore_legacy_tool (DIVERGENT legacy vocabulary 'ball'/'tapered_ball', _ => EndMill), MCP server.rs:452 (canonical serde snake_case, returns Err on unknown). A 4th mechanism is viz's serde-direct ProjectToolSection.tool_type default at io/project.rs:1383. Route all through a single core parse_lenient(&str) -> (ToolType, Option<warning>); thread the warning into viz's existing LoadedProject.warnings (io/project.rs:24, returned :770). Keep EndMill as the loaded value so legacy files still open. Do NOT hard-fail (too harsh for a hobbyist tool; no current precedent). PARITY TRIPWIRE: session/mod.rs:1441 currently asserts parse_tool_type("unknown")==EndMill — any policy change must update this test deliberately. Impact of silent mis-parse: flips ToolGeometryHint::Flat -> changes engaged_diameter_at_doc/mrr_cross_section/chipload family, the wood-adaptive-stepover Flat check (compute/validate.rs:254), and the Scallop ball-tip requirement (compute/execute.rs:1045, compute/catalog.rs:1391). Note: core loader has no warnings channel today — adding one (or returning Result) is part of the unification.
decisions.dissent: Citation correction adopted: the original cutter finding cited a non-existent 'validate.rs:254 Scallop ball-tip gate'; verification refuted that — validate.rs:254 is the wood-adaptive-stepover Flat check, and the real Scallop ball-tip enforcement is at compute/execute.rs:1045 + compute/catalog.rs:1391. Corrected here.

decisions.question: §9 Q5 — Phase 0 finish-op behavior: warning-first vs automatic stock_to_leave mutation for surface-following finish ops.
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: Warning-first. Ship a SuggestWarning (e.g. FinishStockToLeaveRecommended, net-new, warn-only) paired with a rationale entry, NOT auto-mutation of stock_to_leave. Auto-mutation gated behind an explicit SuggestScope, enabled only once in-process leftover stock is available at suggest time. Three converging signals: (1) the 'no background field locking' repo memory — Feeds tab never auto-locks fields, Suggest uses explicit buttons; (2) the established precedent pick_adaptive3d_clearing_strategy (feeds/suggest.rs:1266-1305) is deliberately warn-only, emitting StrategyRecommendedNotApplied (suggest.rs:346); (3) the companion plan itself already DEFERRED automatic 3D-finish stock_to_leave mutation (cutter_axial_constraints_2026-06-06.md:20-23) because it depends on in-process stock the orchestrator can only guess (it would fall back to the rough's stock_to_leave via unwrap_or(0.5) at lines 184-187). STRUCTURAL BLOCKER confirmed: DropCutterConfig has NO stock_to_leave field at all (operation_configs.rs:426-445); Adaptive3dConfig uses stock_to_leave_radial/_axial, not a single field. Mutate only Adaptive3d depth_per_pass and VCarve max_depth (fields that exist and whose per-pass DOC is locally determinable); ProjectCurve depth warn-only.
decisions.dissent: none — suggest-preflight and phase0-axial areas independently reached warning-first with identical evidence.

decisions.question: §9 Q6 — Metrics: typed report preserved (6A) or schema migration to dynamic vector (6B)?
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: 6A (typed report preserved) is the ONLY viable option for this refactor; reject 6B. The consumer set is field-coupled, not state-coupled: the optimizer subsystem (~13 files under tool_load/optimize/ plus strategy/ and retarget/ submodules) computes on gate-specific typed numeric fields — rank.rs:54 reads ChiploadVerdict::Within{approach_to_min,approach_to_max}, delta.rs:155-185 reads approach_to_max.bounds + peak_kw/available_kw, narrative.rs:595-680 reads ChipSide + triggering.bounds, retarget.rs:63-78 and headroom.rs:50-52 read per-gate typed verdicts. A generic Vec<CriterionStatus> (verdict.rs:502, 7 fields incl unmodeled_reason) cannot carry these without per-metric downcasting, which defeats the registry's purpose and does NOT simplify the heaviest consumer. The MCP wire is pure serde passthrough (app/mcp.rs:2471, no field mapping) plus a hardwired typed-shape tool-description string in rs_cam_viz/src/mcp_server.rs, so 6B is a hard public-schema break with no mapping layer to absorb it; 6A additive Option fields (Option + serde(default, skip_serializing_if)) flow through MCP/GUI/serde for free — proven twice (drill_gates commit 47b5864, modulation_summary commit c1a4932). The 6A deliverable should ALSO collapse the two divergent report-assembly sites (tool_load::evaluate_toolpath mod.rs:366 and gcode::project_load_report gcode/mod.rs:371, which have already diverged on modulation_summary) into one, by extending the existing ToolpathLoadContext (mod.rs:323) and threading it into the three gates (deflection 7 args, power 8, chipload 10) and making the gcode site call evaluate_toolpath.
decisions.dissent: none — metrics area's 6A recommendation is strongly evidence-backed and uncontested. Verification corrected '~8 optimizer files' to ~13, 'candidate.rs:48' to :51, CriterionStatus field count 6->7, and gate arg range '8-11' to '7-10'; all corrections incorporated.

decisions.question: §9 Q7 — Dependencies: approve enum_dispatch/bon/strum, or require a no-new-dependency prototype first?
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED (prototype-backed): REJECT strum (the X-macro fully replaces its ALL/EnumIter/EnumCount value with zero deps — proven in /tmp/rscam_xmacro_proto, and gives a free const category() strum can't provide). REJECT enum_dispatch for operations (the heterogeneous Config associated types make it unfit per §3.3; the static registry with fn-pointer generate dispatches fine without it). DEFER bon to an optional later Phase-4 decision — CutterOpProfile is a plain struct/constructor and the workspace already builds large structs with Default+field-init. NET: no new dependencies are needed for the X-macro/registry work. All three are confirmed absent from Cargo.toml and every crates/*/Cargo.toml.
decisions.dissent: none — macro-prototype area built and tested the zero-dep replacement; op-registry concurs.

decisions.question: §9 Q8 — Cutover strategy: one op family at a time vs metadata-only all ops first.
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED: Metadata-only across ALL 23 ops in one Phase 1 PR (guarded by the existing parity tests catalog.rs:1592 operation_catalog_is_exhaustive_and_consistent and session/compute.rs:2715 operation_schema_params_match_params_with_nulls_for_every_op), THEN one family at a time for behavior in Phase 5. Do not mix. Metadata consolidation is uniform and low-risk — spec/param_defs are already wildcard-free exhaustive form, so migrating all 23 at once is mechanical. Behavior cutover is heterogeneous and risky (15-arg execute arms, per-op span/annotate wiring, drill aux pairing via build_drill_op_for_config at execute.rs:76, DrillCycleType->DrillCycle conversion TRIPLICATED at execute.rs:122/135-148/732-745, setup_z_flipped pre-dispatch mutation at TWO sites session/compute.rs:707 and viz compute.rs:119) and benefits from family-at-a-time isolation. Blast radius is small: execute_operation_annotated has only 2 production drivers (session/compute.rs:729, viz worker/execute/mod.rs:132), so a registry-dispatch shim can be proven family-by-family against the retained exhaustive match.
decisions.dissent: none — op-registry recommends this split and verification confirmed the 2-driver blast radius and the triplicated drill conversion.

decisions.question: §9 Q9 — Parity gates: which exact tests/sweeps must pass after each phase?
decisions.recommendation: DECIDED (per-phase, per-crate; NEVER workspace-wide `cargo test` — it loops on this repo). Phase 0: `cargo test -p rs_cam_core -q` + sentries wanaka_axial_doc.rs, agent_search_axial_doc.rs, predicted_feed_gates_f035.rs, constrained_max_modulation_f039.rs. Phase 1: full per-crate suites (core/cli/viz/mcp) anchored by catalog.rs:1592 count + catalog.rs:1601 partition tests and viz job.rs:1299 ToolType-ALL sync; PLUS the two NEW prerequisite nets (schema-field-names-match-serialized-defaults; every-op-has-feeds-hints / no-unintended-(None,None,None)-fallback) which DO NOT EXIST today and must land BEFORE consolidation. Phase 2: per-crate suites + a before/after `cargo test --test param_sweep -- --ignored` fingerprint snapshot (geometry must be byte-identical) + `cargo test -p rs_cam_core --test literature_matrix`. Phase 3: per-crate suites + _litmatrix_scallop_refuses_flat.rs + session/mod.rs:1441 parse_tool_type pin (re-baseline if Q4 lands). Phase 4: wanaka_suggest_integration.rs (NEW/uncommitted; loads real wanaka.toml, exhaustive SuggestWarning catch-all at lines 323-334) is THE gate, backed by the in-crate feeds/suggest.rs test module + literature_matrix harness + lookup_parity.rs/literature_parity.rs. Phase 5: `cargo test --test param_sweep -- --ignored` fingerprint-unchanged is the primary oracle + end_to_end.rs + smoke_baseline_regression_f037.rs + per-family sentries (adaptive3d_*, pocket_lift_bridge_b1.rs, vcarve_lift_bridge_b1.rs). Phase 6: all tool_load/* sentries + drill_metrics_pr2.rs + wanaka_e2e_chipload_gate.rs + diagnostics/tests.rs + MCP serde tests. CRITICAL CAVEATS: param_sweep fingerprints are #[ignore]d (54 tests, run only with --ignored) AND geometry-only (fingerprint.rs derives purely from Toolpath) — they gate Phase 2/5 ONLY and are blind to feeds/suggest/verdict/metadata changes; Phase 1/3/4 parity rests on wanaka_suggest_integration + literature_matrix + catalog count/partition tests, Phase 6 on typed-struct compilation + tool_load sentries + MCP serde.
decisions.dissent: none — parity area answered this comprehensively. Verification corrected line cites (wanaka catch-all 323 not 324; parse_tool_type pin 1441 not 1431; pocket/vcarve sentries carry _b1 suffix) and refused to pin an exact suggest.rs test count; all corrections incorporated.

The real hazard is a naming collision among three feeds/ classifiers (ToolGeometryHint, GeometryClass, proposed CutterKind). v2 Phase 3 explicitly names CutterKind as a cutter-shape classifier and states it is NOT GeometryClass. geometry_class.rs is ALSO added to the §2.1 site inventory as a NEW exhaustive OperationType match (a Phase 2 macro-gen target).

Phase 6 metric scope tier: the v2 plan recommends 6A and distinguishes a 'reporting-only metric' tier (cheap: ~2 production initializers + per-test Option fields) from a 'gating metric' tier (also touches exceeded_criteria/ExceededCriterion/enforce_load_policy/smoke extraction, ~6 extra touch points). The user should confirm whether any near-term planned metric (e.g. SurfaceFinishRa) must gate g-code export, which moves it to the more expensive tier and changes Phase 6 sizing.

CLI legacy job router retirement: cli/job.rs:387-797 is a parallel hand-rolled 6-of-23-op router (pocket/profile/adaptive/rest/adaptive3d/drop-cutter, _ => bail!) that bypasses OperationConfig/execute_operation_annotated entirely, while the modern cli/project.rs uses ProjectSession::generate_all (full 23-op path). The operation registry cannot fix job.rs by consolidation — it needs a rewrite to the ProjectSession path. The user must decide whether to (a) retire/rewrite job.rs as part of this refactor, (b) leave it as a documented permanent divergence, or (c) defer. This is out of scope for the 5 originally-planned agents and is why the v2 plan adds a 6th consumer-surface agent.

ALL_2D/ALL_3D const vs runtime API: the macro-prototype area proved a pure-macro const ALL_2D/ALL_3D split is impractical in macro_rules!; the recommended path keeps the existing &'static [OperationType] consts (catalog.rs:162,176) hand-written, generates category(), and adds a 3-way partition sync test. The alternative (runtime Vec from a category filter) would be a breaking public-API change for consumers expecting &'static slices (viz menus at project_tree.rs:379, toolpath_panel.rs:535). The user should confirm the const-preserving path is acceptable (it is the recommendation) vs accepting an API break for fuller macro generation.

Whether to seal MillingCutter eventually: the v2 plan recommends NOT sealing in Phase 3 and documenting the internal-only contract. If the user wants to formally guarantee external cutter extensibility as a supported API, that is a larger commitment (build_cutter, all three+ IO parsers, and CutterKind would need to stop keying off the closed ToolType enum). Decision deferred to the user; current recommendation is internal-only.

missing_areas.title: Dressup × Operation compatibility matrix (compute/config.rs::for_op / normalize_for_op) had NO investigator
missing_areas.why_it_matters: compute/config.rs:421-531 encodes the operation→dressup-eligibility decision as FIVE separate per-op `matches!(op, ...)` predicates: strip_entry = ProjectCurve|DropCutter (config.rs:464), force_no_entry = Drill|Trace (config.rs:509), prefer_helix = Adaptive (config.rs:514), and a dedicated Adaptive3d entry-strip (config.rs:524). This is exactly the scattered per-op routing the registry is meant to absorb, and it is ALREADY documented (config.rs:539, viz mod.rs:3539) as needing to stay in lockstep with the viz GUI op×dressup-compat table (mod.rs:3540, flagged by the consumers-io investigator) AND with DressupConfig defaults. None of the eight investigators read config.rs's normalize_for_op; the op-registry investigator only saw config.rs via execute.rs. A new op silently inherits the role-default entry style with no compile error and no test forcing a geometric-incompatibility decision — this is a real silent-default the plan's §2.1 (row 9 'dressups') glosses entirely. Critically, the toolpath-IR side is CLEAN (dressup.rs operates purely on Toolpath/AnnotatedToolpath/EntryStyle value types, zero OperationType coupling, verified), so this decision is a pure pre-IR routing concern the registry CAN own without touching the IR boundary — making it an ideal Phase-1/Phase-3 registry field (an `OperationSpec.dressup_policy` or `compatible_entry_styles`).
missing_areas.suggested_followup: Add a §2.1 row for compute/config.rs::normalize_for_op (5 per-op predicates, no compile guard) and scope it as a Phase-1 registry field (dressup/entry-style policy) that the viz op×dressup table (mod.rs:3540) reads from, eliminating the documented 'must match' dual-maintenance between core config.rs:464 and viz mod.rs:3547.

missing_areas.title: The Drill/AlignmentPinDrill (plunge-only / drill-family) classifier is duplicated across 6+ production sites, not 'shared' as §2.1 row 14 claims
missing_areas.why_it_matters: The plan's §2.1 row 14 says is_plunge_only_op is a 'shared helper for drill today', and the op-registry investigator endorsed that it is 'shared across gates (chipload.rs:260, power.rs:92)'. That is materially understated. The identical `OperationType::Drill | OperationType::AlignmentPinDrill` predicate is OPEN-CODED (ignoring the helper) at: power.rs:333 (is_plunge_only_op, the one real helper), tool_load/optimize/mod.rs:147-152, tool_load/optimize/axes.rs:324, session/compute.rs:1706-1710 (sets narrate's is_drill_cycle), plus catalog.rs:503 & :542 group them with DropCutter for transform/air-cut, and feeds/geometry_class.rs:79 groups them with VCarve|ProjectCurve|Trace|Inlay. That is at least four independent re-spellings of the SAME drill-family routing predicate beyond the single shared helper. This is the single highest-value registry-consolidation target the wave undercounted: an `OperationType::is_plunge_only()` / `is_drill_family()` method would dedup the optimizer (twice), the session orchestrator, and the gate helper. Adding a new plunge-only op today silently misroutes through 4+ of these sites with no compile error.
missing_areas.suggested_followup: Re-scope §2.1 row 14 from 'shared helper' to 'duplicated 6+ ways': power.rs:333, optimize/mod.rs:149, optimize/axes.rs:324, session/compute.rs:1706. Make is_plunge_only() a registry/OperationType method in Phase 1 and have all four sites call it; add a test that the helper and the open-coded sites agree.

missing_areas.title: Optimizer per-op axis routing (has_doc_knob, four_variant, OptimizationSurface) are op-addition sites absent from the §2.1 inventory
missing_areas.why_it_matters: The metrics investigator characterized the optimizer's TYPED-FIELD coupling for the 6A/6B fork, and the op-registry investigator noted optimization_surface as one of catalog's ~12 enumerations, but no investigator inventoried the optimizer's per-op AXIS routing as op-addition sites: candidate.rs:96 has_doc_knob is a permissive OPT-IN matches! over 10 ops (a new op silently gets `false` = not DOC-optimizable, no compile error); bounds.rs:351 four_variant = matches!(op_type, Pocket|Adaptive) (silent default for others); bounds.rs:316 resolve_scallop_height_bounds(op_type); grid.rs:85 has_doc_knob(self.op_type). catalog.rs:657 OperationConfig::optimization_surface IS an exhaustive no-wildcard match (good — compile-enforced, the doc-comment at catalog.rs:632 explicitly notes 'no wildcard'), but the optimizer's downstream has_doc_knob/four_variant are silent matches! bools. A new op added to optimization_surface as Optimizable but forgotten in has_doc_knob would silently never search its DOC axis. These belong in the §2.1 op-addition inventory and motivate the registry owning an 'optimizable axes' descriptor.
missing_areas.suggested_followup: Add §2.1 rows for candidate.rs:96 has_doc_knob and bounds.rs:351 four_variant / bounds.rs scallop routing as silent opt-in matches! sites; note optimization_surface (catalog.rs:657) is already exhaustive. Consider a registry field listing each op's optimizable axes so has_doc_knob derives from it.

missing_areas.title: RefusalReason name-collision: the plan invents RefusalReason but the codebase already has RefuseReason (optimizer, serde-public) AND FeedsError (feeds)
missing_areas.why_it_matters: The suggest-preflight and phase0 investigators correctly found that the plan's §3.2/§3.3 `RefusalReason` does not exist and that the feeds feasibility type is FeedsError. But they MISSED that a near-namesake type already exists and is load-bearing: tool_load/mod.rs:100 `pub enum RefuseReason` is a serde-tagged public enum whose own docstring (mod.rs:96-98) says it is 'a superset of the OLD suggest module's refusal kinds plus optimizer-specific ones (NoImprovementFound)'. So the refusal taxonomy was ALREADY unified once (suggest refusals folded into the optimizer's RefuseReason) and is now split between RefuseReason (optimizer, ~10 serde variants incl SimulationRequired/MaterialUnvalidated/NoVendorData/BipolarEngagement) and FeedsError (feeds). The plan introducing a THIRD type literally named `RefusalReason` one letter off from `RefuseReason` is a concrete naming/foot-gun the synthesis must resolve: either reuse FeedsError for preflight feasibility (per the suggest investigator) or explicitly reconcile with the existing serde-public RefuseReason — not invent a collision.
missing_areas.suggested_followup: Replace every plan reference to the invented `RefusalReason` with FeedsError (pre-sim feasibility), and add a note that tool_load/mod.rs:100 RefuseReason is the EXISTING serde-public refusal enum (already a superset of old suggest refusals) — the profile must not shadow it. Flag the 1-letter naming collision explicitly.

missing_areas.title: narrate.rs (agent-facing narrate_toolpath MCP diagnostic) routes on OPERATION-LABEL STRINGS, a brittle uncovered classifier
missing_areas.why_it_matters: narrate.rs is the source of narrate_toolpath, the MCP diagnostic CLAUDE.md tells agents to 'prefer first'. No investigator examined it. narrate.rs:942-951 routes deflection-context text on operation_label STRING literals — Some("3D Finish"), Some("Project Curve"), Some("Drill")|Some("Pin Drill"), Some("VCarve") with a `_ =>` fallback; narrate.rs:1074 has a second operation_label string match; narrate.rs:48/111 carries is_drill_cycle (the duplicated drill predicate again, set at session/compute.rs:1706). missing_areas.title: Cancellation cooperation is asymmetric (only 4 of 23 execute arms consume `cancel`) — relevant to Phase 5 GenerateFn but unaddressed
missing_areas.why_it_matters: The prompt asked specifically about 'cancellation paths through a registry dispatch'. execute_operation_annotated threads cancel: &AtomicBool (execute.rs:254) and only FOUR arms cooperatively poll it via a per-arm closure: Adaptive (execute.rs:428), DropCutter (execute.rs:784/791), Adaptive3d (execute.rs:962/967), Waterline (execute.rs:991/999). The other ~19 arms ignore cancel entirely (fast generators). The metrics and op-registry investigators listed `cancel` as part of the 15-arg signature but never flagged this asymmetry. The implication for Phase 5 is actually DE-RISKING and worth stating: a uniform GenerateFn(&OperationConfig, &ExecutionContext) carrying cancel in the context is MORE consistent than today's per-arm pattern, and only the 4 long-running family adapters must reconstruct the `|| cancel.load(Ordering::SeqCst)` closure — a naive adapter that forgets it would silently make those ops uncancellable (no compile error, only a UX/hang regression not caught by fast unit tests).
missing_areas.suggested_followup: Add a Phase-5 note: only 4 arms (Adaptive/DropCutter/Adaptive3d/Waterline, execute.rs:428/784/962/991) cooperate with cancellation; their GenerateFn adapters must rebuild the cancel closure or the op silently becomes uncancellable.
